facts.fact: The National Police Service's annual report for 2022 says the Digital Occurrence Book, launched on 21 November 2019 at Kasarani Sub-County in Nairobi County, captures the bio-data of crime suspects reported to a police station and the officers assigned, replacing the manual OB there.

The National Police Service says that in 2022 the Digital OB captured reports at the police station on a real-time basis and that senior police commanders could access and monitor its use from their own offices; it gives no number of stations.

The National Police Service's report for 2022 presents the Digital OB as its own system and names its Utumishi Project as the programme that will fully automate the Service, a digitised Occurrence Book among its parts; no budget or funder is given.

systems.tiers: Police station level, launched 21 November 2019 at Kasarani Sub-County, Nairobi; monitored by senior commanders from their offices; no count of stations given

A programme said to lead to full automation of the Service: digitised Occurrence Book, digital HR Information System, digital duty roster and patrol system, and a report generator for crime trends; stated as future

systems.system: digital HR Information System, digital duty roster and patrol system (Utumishi Project)
systems.tiers: Parts of the Utumishi Project; automation said to produce service reports on recruitment, promotion, deployment and transfers

systems.system: report generator for crime trends, with GIS crime mapping (Utumishi Project)
systems.tiers: Part of the Utumishi Project; GIS for crime measurement and mapping to be incorporated
Nairobi (Jogoo House) and Mombasa, installed 2019 by the report's account; used in 2022 chiefly to track stolen or missing vehicles

systems.owner: National Police Service with the World Bank, NTSA and other agencies
Directorate of Criminal Investigations, National Police Service
systems.tiers: One national laboratory, construction completed and opened 2022; ten laboratories including fingerprint identification, ballistics, digital forensics and evidence management

note: The report states no count or share of stations using the Digital OB and names no case-file system. It also says 130 police posts were gazetted as police stations in 2022, without giving the total number of stations.
